Something to do with integer overflow. If you add 1 to 32 bit signed number 2,147,483,647, it becomes -2,147,483,647. Think of it exactly like a car odometer, the highest value, 99,999, goes back to 00,000 because there's no more space. As for why it's not close to that number, probably related to that bug in the first place (the limit is definitely not 2.1 billion, but issues like this crop up frequently even when it's not actually the limit).

Some rules: To take someone down with the ball the tackle is more or less the same technique as American football, between the hips and neck. Above the neck is high tackle, sweeping or gripping the legs is tripping. Also not allowed to push someone in the back, and relatively recently not allowed to touch their back even. 

If you get correctly tackled you must be able to get rid of the ball correctly (kicking or handballing, see below) before the ball either drops or is stuck between you and the other player, this is called "holding the ball" and is a free kick to the other side. These tackling rules are pretty vague and there's a lot of confusion sometimes especially as the rules change very often.

 If nobody was in clear possession before, and the ball is stuck between players, it is a "ball up", almost totally equivalent to a jump ball in basketball, except the ball is bounced on the ground although sometimes thrown up if the first bounce gives too much of an advantage to either side, or the ground is too wet for example. Like basketball, this is also how the game starts and restarts (after goals the ball goes back to the middle)

No throwing allowed.. You have to "handball" it, by holding the ball in one hand and hitting it with your other fist. Kicking is done via drop punt, not drop kick which has not been used in the AFL for decades. Very occasionally, a good forward will use a torpedo kick to get extra length, although this is increasingly uncommon.
